title: The Bakery of Port Alder
premise: Ines Ravensworth, a wedding planner who fled Port Alder twelve years ago after testifying against the family that ruined his father's bakery, returns to plan one last festival wedding and finds himself enrolled in the town's anonymous pen-pal program meant to heal old feuds. His assigned correspondent turns out to be Marisol Vega, the prosecutor's daughter whose testimony once saved him and whose silence afterward broke him. Through letters neither knows are addressed to an enemy, they dismantle each other's versions of the past, until a discovered ledger proves Ines's father was framed by Marisol's own mentor. At the festival's closing night, Ines must choose between public vindication and protecting Marisol from the fallout, choosing instead to tell the truth together—and in doing so, finally forgives the frightened boy in the mirror who ran.
about_author: Vesper Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering courthouse scandals before turning to fiction. They write romances about people who learn that justice and forgiveness rarely arrive by the same door.

chapters.title: Twelve Steps to the Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines returns to Port Alder for a lucrative festival wedding, cataloging his safe routines like armor while avoiding the shuttered bakery that bears his name. The emotional beat is dread disguised as professionalism—he has planned his life so nothing can surprise him.

chapters.title: The Correspondence Act
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The town council's centennial reconciliation program assigns every returning resident an anonymous pen-pal; Ines's first letter arrives scrawled on bakery paper, sharp-tongued and oddly familiar. He writes back out of spite. Beat: reluctant curiosity cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: What Marisol Kept
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Now the town's overworked clerk, Marisol recognizes Ines at the harbor and volunteers as his festival liaison, hiding that she requested him as her pen-pal years of guilt in hand. Beat: the ache of loving someone you helped destroy.

chapters.title: Letters We Never Signed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their letters grow intimate—confessions about fathers, fear, and failure—while their daytime sparring sharpens into flirtation neither will name. A near-kiss in the bakery ruins is interrupted. Beat: two people falling for the same person twice.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Renovating the bakery for the wedding reception, Ines finds his father's hidden ledger proving the 'embezzlement' was fabricated by Judge Aldous Crane—Marisol's mentor and the man she still calls uncle. Beat: rage rekindled, vengeance suddenly possible.

chapters.title: Crane's Quiet Kingdom
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol notices Crane pressuring the council to cancel the festival and quietly bury records; following his trail, she uncovers how much he stole—not just money, but her career's foundation. Beat: loyalty curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At a rehearsal dinner, Crane engineers a confrontation that exposes both secrets at once: the letters' authorship and the ledger's existence. Marisol admits she knew the trial was tainted and stayed silent to survive. Beat: betrayal stacked on betrayal.

chapters.title: Everything He Built to Burn
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Devastated, Ines plans to read the ledger aloud at the festival's closing ceremony, torching Crane publicly even though it will destroy Marisol too. He rehearses his speech in the empty bakery and hears his father's voice asking what it would cost him. Beat: the seduction of righteous cruelty.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the ceremony, Crane preempts them with a smear campaign; when Ines takes the stage, Marisol joins him uninvited and testifies to everything, surrendering her own standing. The town, and the bride whose wedding started it all, choose to hear them. Beat: climax—truth spoken jointly or not at all.

chapters.title: First Batch
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later, Crane faces investigation, the bakery reopens under both their names, and Ines writes one last unsigned letter—then delivers it by hand. Planning weddings again, he books his own date first. Beat: resolution—forgiveness of the man in the mirror.
